To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The N'-mono and double alkylated eremocins were synthesized.

the N'-monoalkylated eremycin derivatives were found to be active against vancomycine-resistant enterococcal strains and that they have the potential to act as transglycosidase inhibitors, which is an alternative to the well known mechanism of glycopeptide antibiotics.

the N'-C10- and N'-C10, N'-C12-alkylated derivatives of eremycin were found to be the most active among the synthesized N'-alkyl derivatives of eremoymcin against vancomycin resistant enterococci and that these compounds have a dual mode of action that doesnot require binding to D-Alanine-D-Alanine.

the development of new glycopeptide antibiotics with improved activity against vancomycin resistant enterococci and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of action of these compounds.
the development of novel antibacterial agents based on the eremomycin scaffold.
the design and synthesis of hydrophobic derivatives of eremycin that have an alternative mechanism inhibiting the transpeptidation stage of bacterial cell-wall biosynthesis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrophobicity of the substituents is a crucial factor in determining the antibacterial activity of eremomycinal derivatives.

the N'-mono and double alkylated derivatives have the potential for the development of new drugs with improved activity against vancomycin resistant bacteria.
